forces.title: UK financial services trade diversifying towards Asia and emerging markets
forces.description: The UK's financial services trade, including asset management, is gradually shifting beyond its traditional anchors (EU, US) towards faster-growing economies in Asia-Pacific, Hong Kong, Japan, Singapore, China, and the GCC. This diversification provides new commercial opportunities and enhances the UK's economic resilience by spreading exposure across multiple global markets, reducing dependency on any single region. This requires active nurturing to convert into commercial opportunity.
forces.source_title: Global financial services trade in transition

forces.title: Asset managers leveraging AI to transform operations and drive value
forces.description: Agentic AI is emerging as a critical tool for asset managers to overcome industry challenges like fee compression and rising costs. By integrating AI into core workflows, firms can significantly expand investment research coverage (2x-5x), personalize client interactions, accelerate new product development (2x-3x), reduce trade errors (50%-70%), and achieve substantial cost reductions (25%-30% over 3-5 years), leading to a P&L value uplift of 300-500 bps.

forces.title: Structural fee compression challenges asset management profitability
forces.description: The asset management industry is experiencing persistent fee compression, ranging from 1% to 3% annually, which is eroding profit margins. This is compounded by costs consistently outpacing revenues for the past 15 years, leading to a growing gap between revenue and cost growth rates (5.1% vs 5.4%). This structural pressure necessitates efficiency gains and innovative value propositions to maintain profitability and reverse negative operating leverage, pushing firms towards AI adoption.

forces.title: European retirement crisis presents significant market opportunity for asset managers
forces.description: Europe's aging population and declining public pension replacement rates are creating a substantial and growing gap in retirement income. Despite consumer anxiety, private retirement savings are underdeveloped due to low awareness and lack of activation. This represents an opportunity for asset managers to engage early, provide personalized guidance, offer decumulation solutions, and build long-term relationships as trusted retirement partners, capitalizing on a large underserved market, as exemplified by the UK's deep defined-contribution market.
forces.source_title: Europe’s Retirement Crisis Is an Opportunity for Insurers and Asset Managers

forces.title: Asset managers lag behind banks and fintechs in AI maturity
forces.description: Asset managers are trailing banks and fintechs in their adoption and maturity of AI solutions, with most firms not having moved beyond pilot stages. This delay puts them at a disadvantage in capturing compounding advantages from AI, potentially leading to missed opportunities for enhanced productivity, client engagement, and new product development that industry leaders and tech providers are already seizing. This gap could hinder their ability to address structural fee compression and rising costs.

forces.title: Investor demand for AI capabilities drives asset management innovation
forces.description: Institutional allocators, wealth managers, and a growing percentage of retail investors are actively seeking or using AI-powered tools for investment research and decision-making. This strong demand from various client segments is compelling asset managers to accelerate their AI journey, fostering innovation and adoption of advanced technologies to meet evolving client expectations and maintain competitiveness. Firms without AI tools face a talent disadvantage as younger professionals expect AI capabilities.

forces.title: Private equity value creation shifts to operational performance focus
forces.description: The private equity industry is moving away from value creation primarily driven by leverage and multiple expansion. With deal multiples at record highs and hold periods extending to over six and a half years, PE firms must increasingly rely on improving portfolio companies' operating performance. This necessitates adopting a more adaptive, execution-led model focused on enterprise transformation, re-underwriting value, and strategic use of AI to drive sustained value and faster exits.
forces.source_title: Unlocking full potential: Five practices reshaping PE value creation

forces.title: AI integration boosts private equity portfolio company valuations and efficiency
forces.description: Private equity-backed companies that broadly embed AI across their operations, products, and new business ventures achieve significantly higher revenue multiples (130% higher) and greater revenue per employee ($180,000 increase). This demonstrates AI's role as a powerful catalyst for value creation beyond mere productivity gains, offering PE firms a strategic advantage in a challenging market by enhancing competitive positioning, driving growth, and improving commercial metrics like customer retention and average order value.
forces.source_title: Beyond productivity: How AI creates value in private equity

forces.title: Climate-driven insurability challenges threaten asset valuations and investment
forces.description: Rising physical climate risks are straining insurance markets, leading to higher premiums, tighter terms, and reduced capacity. This widening 'protection gap' transmits into capital markets by increasing operating costs for assets, reducing their attractiveness to investors, and impacting cash flows. For asset managers, this poses a risk to asset valuations and the investability of physical assets, potentially leading to 'stranded assets' and slower economic recovery, especially in real estate and infrastructure sectors.
forces.source_title: Mind the protection gap: The risk to capital markets and the resilience financing imperative

forces.title: Financial 'tragedy of horizons' hinders long-term adaptation investments
forces.description: Financial decision-making is often constrained by short-term horizons (e.g., 3-5 year investment cycles), which clashes with the long-term nature of climate risk and adaptation benefits. Resilience investments, deriving value from avoided future losses, are often heavily discounted, appearing less attractive on a risk-adjusted return basis. This creates a structural disincentive for asset managers and investors to allocate capital to long-term adaptation measures, biasing capital towards mitigation or revenue-generating infrastructure.
forces.source_title: Mind the protection gap: The risk to capital markets and the resilience financing imperative

forces.title: Early-life wealth building programs open new market for asset managers
forces.description: Initiatives focused on early-life wealth building, such as the UK Child Trust Fund or proposed 'Trump accounts' (530A accounts), create opportunities for asset managers to administer and integrate investment accounts into existing financial behaviors. By simplifying account design, reducing fees, standardizing default options, and enabling automated contributions, asset managers can capture new client segments and facilitate long-term asset accumulation, particularly for households with fewer resources, thereby shaping economic mobility.
forces.source_title: From access to assets: How early-life wealth building can shape economic mobility

forces.title: Purchase price discipline becomes crucial for PE fund returns
forces.description: Following a period of cheap financing and expanding deal multiples (2010-2017), macroeconomic tailwinds for private equity have diminished (2018-2023). This has made purchase price multiples (PPM) a more critical determinant of returns for buyout funds, with disciplined buyers in the lowest-price quartile significantly outperforming those who paid higher multiples (5.5x MOIC vs 3.6x MOIC for top performers in recent vintages). This highlights a heightened risk of overpaying for assets, especially for durable, 'A-grade' businesses.
forces.source_title: Private equity confirms a timeless principle: Purchase price matters

viewpoints.title: UK asset management well-positioned for global growth in emerging markets
viewpoints.description: The UK's financial services trade, including asset management, is diversifying beyond its traditional EU and US anchors towards faster-growing economies in Asia-Pacific, Hong Kong, Japan, Singapore, China, and the GCC. TheCityUK highlights that UK capabilities are relevant to these emerging demands, creating commercial opportunities. This diversification is seen as a strategic asset, enhancing economic resilience by spreading exposure to economic or regulatory shocks across multiple global markets. Active nurturing is required as global demand, capital flows, and regulatory approaches shift.
viewpoints.source_title: Global financial services trade in transition

viewpoints.title: Europe's retirement crisis offers significant growth opportunity for asset managers
viewpoints.description: BCG identifies a large, underserved, and growing retirement savings market in Europe, where public pensions are increasingly insufficient. Despite widespread anxiety about retirement, private savings remain underdeveloped due to behavioral barriers and lack of market activation. Asset managers are urged to reposition from product providers to trusted lifetime partners, utilizing AI for personalized guidance and addressing broader needs beyond core savings, including decumulation and wealth management, to capture this significant opportunity across the customer’s lifetime.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe’s Retirement Crisis Is an Opportunity for Insurers and Asset Managers

viewpoints.title: Agentic AI crucial for asset managers to overcome margin pressure and drive value
viewpoints.description: The asset management industry faces structural challenges like persistent fee compression and costs outpacing revenues. BCG asserts that Agentic AI is an inflection point, offering opportunities to expand investment coverage (2x-5x), increase client coverage (up to 3x), and unlock significant operational capacity (55%-65%). Leaders are pulling away from laggards, with AI-first asset managers expected to capture 300-500 bps of value, transforming profitability and potentially shifting margins from 30% to over 40% by reversing negative operating leverage.

viewpoints.title: PE firms must adopt adaptive, execution-led models for value creation
viewpoints.description: The private equity industry is experiencing a recovery, but traditional value creation drivers such as leverage and multiple expansion are diminishing. With valuation multiples at record highs and hold periods extending, PE firms must increasingly focus on improving the operating performance of portfolio companies. Leading firms are now 're-underwriting' value during the hold period, embracing enterprise transformation, investing in dedicated transformation leadership, mobilizing employees, and building AI into a portfolio-wide value creation engine to drive faster exits and higher valuations.
viewpoints.source_title: Unlocking full potential: Five practices reshaping PE value creation

viewpoints.title: Broad AI adoption in PE-backed companies significantly boosts revenue multiples
viewpoints.description: Private equity-backed companies that comprehensively integrate AI across operations, products, and new business ventures achieve median revenue multiples 130% higher than those focusing solely on productivity. McKinsey's analysis indicates AI is an underutilized catalyst for revenue growth, particularly crucial given the industry's exit backlog and modest returns. Businesses progressing to higher AI maturity levels (embedding AI in products, building new ventures) observe substantial increases in revenue per employee and valuation, transforming commercial performance and competitive positioning beyond mere efficiency gains.
viewpoints.source_title: Beyond productivity: How AI creates value in private equity

demand_drivers.description: Driven 80%+ of revenue growth in 2025 for the asset management industry.
Institutional allocators are asking about AI in due diligence, wealth managers are partnering with AI firms, and 12-15% of retail investors use GenAI for investing decisions.

pnl_drivers.description: Structural erosion of 1% to 3% annually, impacting profit margins. Active ETFs charge 37% less than active mutual funds.
For the last 15 years, asset management costs (5.4% CAGR) have outpaced revenues (5.1% CAGR), contributing to margin pressure.

new_opportunities.description: Can unlock capacity in operations of 55% to 65%, expand investment coverage by 2x-5x, increase client coverage per relationship manager by up to 3x, and generate 300-500 bps of value across the P&L.
Agentic AI can enable 2x-3x speed to market for new products.
Agentic AI can drive up to a 1% uplift in net inflows, with ~65% of this uplift from win rate and coverage gains.

market_sizing.methodology: Global Assets Under Management (AUM) for the asset management industry, growing 11% primarily from market performance. Fee compression is structural at 1-3% annually, and costs have outpaced revenues for 15 years.

demand_drivers.description: Europe's population is aging, and its workforce is shrinking, impacting the sustainability of public pension systems.
The average new pension as a share of gross wage at retirement across the EU is forecast to fall by 4 percentage points, from 45% in 2022 to 41% by 2045.
Most Europeans are anxious about retirement but lack awareness of private savings products, with advisors not actively engaging. Only 18% of European consumers own a personal pension product.

new_opportunities.description: Engaging customers early at key life moments, providing personalized guidance using agentic AI, and delivering value during the retirement transition with decumulation solutions and consolidation tools.

Developing long-term, high-value relationships with retirees by offering wealth management advice, ongoing financial guidance, and protection products, extending into the broader 'silver economy' through partnerships.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of European private retirement savings markets, highlighting that the UK has the continent's deepest defined-contribution market. CAGRs are provided for specific EU countries as indicators of regional growth potential.
market_sizing.source_title: Europe’s Retirement Crisis Is an Opportunity for Insurers and Asset Managers

pnl_drivers.description: AI can improve average revenue per user, customer lifetime value, customer retention, and repayment rates.

AI can streamline sales, automate customer service and onboarding, and generate marketing content, leading to higher revenue per employee ($180,000 increase, 52% jump from level three for level four companies).

new_opportunities.description: Companies at this level trade at a median revenue multiple of 20x (43% higher than level two), by optimizing pricing, personalizing customer experiences, improving win rates, and reducing churn.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Embedding AI in products and services (Level 3)

new_opportunities.description: Companies using AI to create new business ventures achieve the highest median revenue multiple of 31x (2023-2025).

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of 471 PE-backed companies across 31 industries (including financial services), focusing on AI maturity levels and their impact on revenue multiples and revenue per employee for deals completed from 2023 onward.
market_sizing.source_title: Beyond productivity: How AI creates value in private equity
